speaker: Muse
text: Your $100 US / Rs10k India budget can’t realistically get an IPO allotment – US IPOs need hundreds per lot and Indian IPOs need a full lot worth far more than $10, and allotment is lottery-like so expected value is tiny after the lock-up. On Zerodha delivery for Reliance.NS the round-trip cost on Rs10,000 is about 0.38% ~Rs38 with zero brokerage, plus 20% short-term capital gains tax if you sell within 12 months or 12.5% long-term after the exemption, and you can only buy whole shares so price must be under Rs10k per share.

speaker: Kimi K3
text: SYNA's fundamentals don't match the momentum: four straight quarters of operating losses with margins stuck between -2.8% and -8.1%, and insiders have sold $5.2M with zero buys in six months. Wells Fargo just downgraded to Equal-Weight with a $123 target, which is basically where the stock sits now after today's 14% pop on 8x volume. For a $100 account chasing 10x, this is a momentum trade disguised as an investment — the 77.8% one-year CAGR looks great until you see the -85% max drawdown and -7.9% five-year CAGR. On the India side, your Rs 10k can't touch auto or battery names like Tata Motors (Rs 900+) or Exide (Rs 400+) for meaningful position sizes after the 0.38% round-trip cost; you'd own 11 shares of Tata Motors and a 1% move barely covers fees. Fractional US shares solve this — $100 buys you 0.43 shares of NVDA or 0.12 shares of TSLA with zero commission, so the compounding math actually works. IPO allotments remain a lottery: US needs $500+ per lot, India needs Rs 15k+ per lot, and your budgets get zero allocation.
